source_review.notes: Checked twelve primary sources: the original Google MapReduce publication; current Apache Hadoop tutorial/default configuration; Apache Spark shuffle configuration, RDD, tuning, and SQL tuning documentation; Apache Flink batch shuffle, ExternalSorter API, configuration, and ORDER BY documentation; and current Dask shuffle documentation. All twelve URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date. Sources support shuffle sorting, comparators/grouping, spill/merge, bypass, destination clustering, external sorting, and result-order distinctions.

evidence: Reviewed exchange comparator relation, records N, runs S, fan-in F, passes P, destination offsets, file length, comparator equality, grouping equality, and multiset union.
Checked destination clustering, per-partition key order, secondary order, tie order, stability, and global order remain distinct.
Checked partition, grouping, comparison, normalization, null/NaN, collation, serialization, attempt, and format identities are used consistently.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Ordering notation and complexity bounds have explicit assumptions; implementation thresholds are not presented as universal.

evidence: Executed sorted-run-merge with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced 18 input/output records in nondecreasing order from four runs.
Checked destination offsets (0,120,120,500) yield block lengths 120, 0, and 380 bytes.
Recomputed 64 runs at fan-in eight and 20 runs at fan-in five as two balanced passes.
Confirmed the fixture output is the integers 1 through 18 with no omissions or duplicates.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The executable fixture validates integer k-way merge only, not byte indexes, external I/O, attempts, or arbitrary comparators.

evidence: Verified balanced initial run sorting gives S times O((N/S) log(N/S)) = O(N log(N/S)).
Verified one heap merge pass uses O(N log F) comparisons and O(F) heads plus bounded buffers, with P=ceil(log_F S) balanced passes.
Reviewed the inductive least-head proof for sorted multiset union and exact-once advancement.
Checked partition-first ordering implies contiguous destination ranges and monotonic offsets, but not key or global order.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Complexity claims exclude comparator/key-width constants, decoding/allocation, uneven runs, I/O, compression, and failures.

evidence: Reviewed empty/one-record/already/reverse ordered inputs, all-equal keys, empty destinations, giant keys, long common prefixes, and skewed runs/groups.
Reviewed nulls, NaNs, signed zero, overflow, invalid text, Unicode normalization, collation/locale changes, composite ties, and missing tie-breakers.
Reviewed corrupt/missing/truncated runs and indexes, comparator exceptions/nontransitivity, descriptor limits, disk-full, cancellation, process loss, retry, and speculation.
Reviewed bypass with/without ordering, binary-object disagreement, mixed comparator versions, compression framing, unsafe combine, and sensitive min/max keys.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Sortedness, reproducibility, partition correctness, multiset preservation, durability, and security can fail independently.

evidence: Traced records through pinned partition/sort tuple, serialized pointer buffer, immutable sorted spill, bounded merge, destination index, candidate file, accepted attempt, and publication.
Checked every run uses one comparator identity and merge emits every input once in nondecreasing order.
Checked offsets begin at zero, remain monotonic, end at file length, and preserve destination membership and compression restartability.
Checked grouping/partition compatibility, combiner algebra, attempt isolation, bounded resources, error propagation, and cleanup lifecycle.
invariant_checking.notes: Checksums establish byte integrity only; order and comparator compatibility require separate validation.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from ordering contract and partition compatibility through run formation, merge, indexes, optional paths, attempts, metrics, tests, and governance.
Checked the k-way merge proof premises include individually sorted complete inputs, consistent total comparator, correct heap, exact advancement, immutable inputs, and output error handling.
Checked partition contiguity proof requires destination as the first sort component.

Reviewed counterexamples for global-sort claims, clustering-as-key-order, comparator edge cases, distributed stability, checksum semantics, unlimited fan-in, secondary partitioning, bypass equivalence, and version mixing.
proof_review.notes: Deterministic byte output is explicitly stronger than valid sortedness and requires full tie-break and serialization semantics.

evidence: Audited uses of sorted, total, stable, deterministic, global, compatible, exact, complete, accepted, bounded, valid, and reproducible.
Confirmed destination-only sort is labeled clustering and not a user-key or global-order guarantee.
Confirmed comparison/pass bounds are asymptotic simplified models and current engine bypass/sort behavior is sourced.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No sorting algorithm, comparator representation, fan-in, bypass threshold, or persistence design is claimed universally optimal.

evidence: Reviewed proposed record/key byte, comparator, prefix fallback, allocation, run, sort, merge, I/O, fan-in, file, compression, combine, block-distribution, and bypass metrics.
Confirmed no universal key encoding, algorithm, fan-in, memory, spill size, comparator cost, threshold, collation, or retention period is prescribed.
Checked mean, tail, maximum, per-attempt, per-run, partition-only, key-order, and global-order evidence remain distinct.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production choices require representative key distributions, comparator/serializer behavior, memory, disks, downstream contracts, failures, and policy.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed sort-based shuffle from semantic ordering promises through comparator compatibility, binary/object comparison, run formation, k-way merge, indexes, grouping/combining, secondary sort, bypass, skew, attempts, validation, and governance.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed practical sort tuples, normalized comparison, pointer buffers, immutable runs, fan-in planning, offset validation, compression frames, failure handling, upgrade tests, telemetry, key redaction, and lifecycle. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from ordering contracts and comparators through external mechanics, proofs, optional paths, failure, and governance. Ten examples and five complete answers cover tuple order, normalization, heap merge, indexes, secondary sort, collation, fan-in, bypass, speculation, and adversarial testing.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Spark, Flink, Hadoop, or Dask maintainer, sorting/algorithms researcher, database/runtime/storage specialist, Unicode/collation expert, security/privacy/legal/records authority, affected-user reviewer, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
